public.text: Treating interoperability as a property of the whole rather than a component is one of the most useful clarifications in the draft, and it appears as a boundary note in the component chapter. In many countries, including the Netherlands, interoperability is organised as a succession of projects with start and end dates, which is the direct cause of capability that appears and then lapses.
public.suggestedRevision: Elevate this into the DPI-H principles in section 1.4 and state the practical consequence: because interoperability is a property and not a deliverable, it cannot be financed as a project and must be funded and governed as a standing capability. This gives countries a concrete test - if interoperability has a completion date in their plan, it is being treated as a component.
